head_commit.message:
[app-server] feat: v2 apply_patch approval flow  (#6760)

This PR adds the API V2 version of the apply_patch approval flow, which
centers around `ThreadItem::FileChange`.

This PR wires the new RPC (`item/fileChange/requestApproval`, V2 only)
and related events (`item/started`, `item/completed` for
`ThreadItem::FileChange`, which are emitted in both V1 and V2) through
the app-server
protocol. The new approval RPC is only sent when the user initiates a
turn with the new `turn/start` API so we don't break backwards
compatibility with VSCE.

Similar to https://github.com/openai/codex/pull/6758, the approach I
took was to make as few changes to the Codex core as possible,
leveraging existing `EventMsg` core events, and translating those in
app-server. I did have to add a few additional fields to
`EventMsg::PatchApplyBegin` and `EventMsg::PatchApplyEnd`, but those
were fairly lightweight.

However, the `EventMsg`s emitted by core are the following:
```
1) Auto-approved (no request for approval) 
- EventMsg::PatchApplyBegin
- EventMsg::PatchApplyEnd

2) Approved by user
- EventMsg::ApplyPatchApprovalRequest
- EventMsg::PatchApplyBegin

head_commit.message:
Fix: Skip intermediate assistant messages between tool_calls and tool responses

This fix ensures that assistant messages appearing between tool_calls 
and tool responses are skipped to comply with OpenAI API requirements.

The issue occurred when intermediate assistant messages were inserted 
between tool_calls and their responses, violating the API's message 
ordering requirements and causing tool call failures with strict API 
providers.

Changes:
- Add awaiting_tool_response flag to track tool call state
- Skip intermediate assistant messages when awaiting tool response
- Reset flag when tool response is received
- Apply to FunctionCall, LocalShellCall, and CustomToolCall

Test Results:
- 100 tests passed
- 3 tests failed (pre-existing issues in official codebase)

Fixes tool call failures by maintaining proper message ordering:
assistant (with tool_calls) → tool (response)
